If no request has occurred, describe established response readiness without inventing an accounting or historical evidence. An incident log is not an accounting of information held.
questions.topic: Requested accounting of personal information held
questions.remediation: Resolve gaps in accounting for the personal information held about a requester.

questions.prompt: When an applicable request is made, are people actually given an accounting of disclosures of their personal information?
questions.help: Assess fulfillment using relevant disclosure records, not just their availability. A required accounting left undelivered is incomplete performance. If no request has occurred, describe established response readiness without inventing an accounting or historical evidence. This differs from giving a data copy or reporting only unauthorized disclosures.
questions.remediation: Resolve gaps in providing requested disclosure accounting.

P7.1.title: Personal-data accuracy
P7.1.objective: Understand accurate, current, complete, and relevant personal information in relation to its intended privacy purpose.

questions.prompt: Is personal information collected and maintained with accuracy suitable for its intended purpose?
questions.help: Describe suitable checks and handling of reported errors. Appropriate manual review or technical validation may be used without demanding one universal verification source.
questions.remediation: Address inaccurate personal information or inadequate error handling.

questions.prompt: Is personal information kept sufficiently current for the purpose it serves?
questions.help: Explain how needed updates reach the relevant records and responsibilities. Do not impose a universal refresh interval unrelated to the purpose.
questions.remediation: Resolve outdated personal information that impairs its intended purpose.

questions.prompt: Is personal information complete enough for its intended purpose?
questions.help: Describe how missing information that matters to the purpose is addressed. Completeness does not mean collecting every possible personal detail.
questions.remediation: Address missing personal information that is necessary for the intended purpose.

questions.prompt: Is the personal information collected and maintained relevant to the privacy objectives?
questions.help: Explain how irrelevant information is recognized and handled. A larger or more detailed dataset is not automatically better or more appropriate.
questions.remediation: Resolve collection or maintenance of personal information unrelated to the privacy purposes.

P8.1.title: Complaints and privacy monitoring
P8.1.objective: Understand a working privacy inquiry and dispute process, periodic compliance monitoring, and prompt correction of deficiencies.

questions.prompt: Is a process implemented to receive and address privacy inquiries, complaints, and disputes from people and others?
questions.help: Describe how concerns reach responsible people and are taken up. A mailbox or isolated ad hoc response is not necessarily an implemented process; a dedicated complaints platform is not required.
questions.remediation: Implement a workable process for receiving and addressing privacy inquiries, complaints, and disputes.

questions.prompt: Does that process resolve the matters and communicate their resolution appropriately?
questions.help: Explain decisions and communication to the relevant person or party, including controller arrangements. Closing an internal record without communicating the resolution is a different outcome.
questions.remediation: Resolve gaps in addressing matters to resolution and communicating the outcome.

questions.prompt: Is compliance with privacy objectives monitored periodically?
questions.help: Describe the actual monitoring approach and coverage. Periodic monitoring is part of the criterion, but no universal annual or quarterly interval is prescribed.
questions.remediation: Establish or improve periodic monitoring of compliance with privacy objectives.

questions.prompt: Are identified deficiencies corrected and other necessary actions taken promptly?
questions.help: Explain responsibility and follow-through. An open action or accepted risk is not automatic evidence that a necessary correction occurred; if no deficiency has been found, describe the established response.
questions.remediation: Address delayed or missing correction and follow-through on privacy deficiencies.
